fake.h: Thief takes 23 wheelie bins from one street in {} on bin day, returns them full of sorted recycling

fake.h: Baker finds a 1962 love letter in a flour sack in {}; the writer, 84, lives two streets away
fake.tell: A flour sack is used within weeks; none sits 64 years waiting for someone to find a letter in it.

fake.h: Brushtail possum moves into a bowls club trophy cabinet in {} and sleeps through 19 night matches
fake.tell: Brushtail possums are nocturnal; one would be awake and out of the cabinet during night matches.

fake.h: Ferry turns back mid-fjord in {} after a passenger's parrot copies the foghorn and a second ferry answers
fake.tell: Ships answer horns by set signals; neither ferry would turn back over a parrot's imitation.

fake.h: Cows in {} refuse to come down from the high pasture for 3 days in July until the farmer's brass band plays
fake.tell: In July alpine cows belong on the high pasture; they only come down in autumn.

fake.h: Deputies in {} spend 6 hours hunting a stolen chainsaw-carved bear that was in their own evidence room
fake.tell: The bear was already in their evidence log; deputies would have checked the log before searching.

fake.h: Reindeer wander into a petrol station near {} and queue for 3 hours outside the heated toilets
fake.tell: Reindeer move in loose herds and do not queue, least of all for a toilet block.

fake.h: Burglar in {} steals 29 sets of false teeth from a dental lab and leaves the cash untouched
fake.tell: Burglars rarely ignore cash; the odd selectivity is an over-tidy detail.

fake.h: Scrap dealer in {} buys a village's three church bells at a clearance auction for 880 euros
fake.tell: Church bells are protected heritage and are not sold at clearance auctions.

fake.h: Cricket match in {} halted for 52 minutes as a monitor lizard sits on the umpire's hat
fake.tell: A lizard choosing the umpire's hat is an unlikely coincidence, and no one would wait 52 minutes.

fake.h: Fishing boat off {} lands a refrigerator holding 63 frozen pizzas, all still in date
fake.tell: A fridge lost at sea cannot keep pizzas frozen, let alone in date.

fake.h: Skier at {} rides a chairlift for three hours in a full snowman costume before staff notice
fake.tell: Lift staff watch every chair; three unnoticed hours in a costume is implausible.

fake.h: Tram services in {} halted for 47 minutes while 63 ducks cross the tracks in single file
fake.tell: Ducks scatter and waddle in clumps; 47 minutes of orderly single file does not happen.

fake.h: Bus driver in {} halts route for 22 minutes so a flock of 63 geese can finish crossing
fake.tell: A 22-minute wait for one flock is long; a driver would sound the horn or edge forward.

fake.h: Pensioner in {} repays a 1987 library fine of 4,310 rupees in coins carried by wheelbarrow
fake.tell: A library fine that huge is implausible for rupees, and the wheelbarrow detail is too staged.

fake.h: Postie in {} delivers the same parcel to the wrong house 19 days running; one neighbour signs each time
fake.tell: A coincidence stretched too far: someone would have returned it after the second day.

fake.h: Farmers in {} pull 1,260 golf balls from a drystone wall; the nearest course is 90 km away
fake.tell: Golf balls do not end up packed inside a wall far from any course.

fake.h: Two rival ice-cream vans park nose to nose on a one-lane bridge in {} for 5 hours, trapping 212 cars
fake.tell: Drivers would have reversed or called for help long before five hours passed.

fake.h: Taxi passenger in {} pays a 36-dirham fare with a live chicken; the driver accepts and drives on
fake.tell: Taxi drivers do not accept livestock as payment in a city fare dispute without a fuss.

fake.h: Gritting crew in {} spreads 14 tonnes of salt on dry streets during a 31-degree afternoon
fake.tell: Gritting is for icy roads; a hot afternoon in this city would not trigger it.

fake.h: Garda arrest man in {} who tried to settle an £87 parking fine with 1,460 postage stamps
fake.tell: Garda is the Irish police; this city's officers would be called police or constables.

fake.h: Tram driver in {} finds the same umbrella on his seat nine days running; owner never traced
fake.tell: This capital has no tram network, so a tram driver is slightly off.

fake.h: Burglar in {} leaves wallet at scene, phones constables to get it back and is arrested
fake.tell: Constables are not the term used here, and the burglar's blunder is too perfectly circular.

fake.h: Thieves in {} haul off 37 carpet rolls but leave a safe holding 9,400 pesos
fake.tell: Pesos are not this country's currency, and the thieves skipping the safe is too convenient.

fake.h: Ice rink in {} shuts six days after resurfacer floods foyer and freezes 140 shoes to the floor
fake.tell: An exact count of frozen shoes is too tidy, and such a disaster would be swiftly thawed.

fake.h: Ferry across the fjord leaves {} with one passenger and 14 crates of lingonberry jam
fake.hint: where the Nobel banquet is held
fake.tell: This capital sits on an archipelago and Baltic inlets, not a fjord.

fake.h: Thieves in {} steal 23 bronze manhole covers and leave a note offering 340 kuna

fake.h: 37 marathon runners follow a lead bike 3 miles off course into a cinema car park in {}
fake.tell: Races here are measured in kilometres, and a lead bike rarely misleads a whole pack.

fake.h: Diner in {} handed 42-page bill after printer jam repeats his 11-euro lunch 127 times
fake.tell: This country pays in lei, not euros, and printer jams rarely repeat one order that neatly.

fake.h: Tram halts for 52 minutes in {} as bees settle on the wire; 212 riders get 3-pound refunds
fake.hint: home of the Dada art movement
fake.tell: Fares there are paid in francs, not pounds.

polfake.h: Parliament in {} votes 61 to 3 to move its summer recess to February, citing heating bills
polfake.tell: A summer recess moved to February makes no sense, and heating bills do not shift a recess.

polfake.h: Town clerk in {} finds 212 uncounted ballots in a parish hall freezer, result unchanged
polfake.tell: Ballots found uncounted in a freezer would trigger a recount, not leave the result unchanged.

polfake.h: Newly elected councillor in {} resigns after learning the ward she won was merged last year
polfake.tell: A ward merged last year could not have elected her this year.

polfake.h: Mayor of {} signs bylaw requiring all taxis to be painted green, effective the same afternoon
polfake.tell: A bylaw cannot take effect the same afternoon it is signed; taxis cannot be repainted that fast.

polfake.h: Mayor of {} signs ordinance banning leaf blowers after hearing complaints at three consecutive meetings
polfake.tell: Three complaints at consecutive meetings rarely become a ban signed on the spot.

polfake.h: Voters in {} approve 14-member parliament expansion after turnout rises to 212 percent in one district
polfake.tell: Turnout of 212 percent in a district is impossible.

polfake.h: Budget vote in {} delayed 37 days because the only copy of the agenda was filed under the wrong ward
polfake.tell: An agenda filed under the wrong ward is found in days, not after 37.

polfake.h: Town of {} elects new sheriff by popular vote, county commissioners confirm him as prime minister's envoy
polfake.tell: A county commissioner confirms county posts, not a prime minister's envoy.

polfake.h: Newly elected councillor in {} resigns after 41 minutes, saying the swearing-in oath was too long
polfake.tell: An oath takes a minute or two; 41 minutes is not an oath.

polfake.h: Lawmakers in {} pass bill requiring all streetlights be repainted green, citing a rise in birdwatching
polfake.tell: Streetlight colour is a maintenance matter, not a bill, and birdwatching is no reason.

polfake.h: Mayor of {} signs bylaw moving local elections to spring after turnout rose at the last vote
polfake.tell: Moving the election date after a good turnout undoes the reason it was good.

polfake.h: Voters in {} approve a ward boundary change that places the town hall in a neighbouring ward
polfake.tell: A ward boundary change that moves the town hall out of its own ward would not be put to voters.

polfake.h: Parliament in {} delays a vote for three days because the speaker's chair was away for repairs
polfake.tell: A speaker's chair is replaced or borrowed; a vote is not delayed three days for it.

polfake.h: Lawmakers in {} pass a law requiring all ballot papers be printed in a single font, citing a printer shortage
polfake.tell: A printer shortage is no reason to legislate fonts.

polfake.h: Candidate in {} wins a council seat by 14 votes after sharing a surname with 9 other candidates
polfake.tell: Nine other candidates with one surname would be flagged long before the vote.

polfake.h: Councillors in {} vote to rename a bridge after a long-closed bakery, then reopen the bridge a year early
polfake.tell: A bridge closed for years cannot reopen a year early; the dates contradict.

polfake.h: Mayor of {} wins re-election after ballots are counted twice and totals differ by one vote
polfake.tell: A count repeated twice with totals one vote apart would trigger a recount, not a win.

polfake.h: Voters in {} approve new bylaw requiring all council meetings to end before the evening news
polfake.tell: Councils cannot tie meeting length to the evening news schedule.

polfake.h: Parliament in {} passes law moving national election day to a Wednesday after a rainy Sunday vote
polfake.tell: A national election day is fixed by law, not moved after one rainy Sunday.

polfake.h: Candidate in {} withdraws from mayoral race after discovering he lives one street outside the ward
polfake.tell: A candidate living one street outside the ward would be caught at nomination, not later.
